title: monday.com implementation: monday CRM setup | Stacktik
metaDescription: monday.com implementation for sales teams: monday CRM pipeline, lead routing, calling, dashboards and training, scoped in writing for a fixed fee.
h1: A monday.com implementation built around how your team sells.
lede: A monday.com implementation for a sales team turns monday CRM, the sales CRM from monday.com, into the system the team runs on: boards and pipeline, forms routed to reps, automations, calling and email connected, dashboards, and training.

summary.label: What it is
summary.text: Setting up monday CRM, the sales CRM from monday.com: boards, pipeline, forms, automations and dashboards built around your sales process, then the team trained.

summary.label: Who it is for
summary.text: Sales and customer-facing teams that bought monday CRM, or are deciding on it, and want it set up properly by one person.

summary.label: What you get
summary.text: A pipeline with written stage rules, leads routed to reps, calling and email connected, dashboards, recorded training and handover notes.

summary.label: How it is priced
summary.text: The software is per seat, on monday.com's own plans. Stacktik's implementation is a separate fixed fee, quoted in writing before work starts.

blocks.intro: Every project is scoped on a written proposal, so this is the list Stacktik draws from, not a fixed package.

items.title: Boards and pipeline
items.body: Pipeline stages set up on the boards your reps work from, with written rules for when an opportunity moves forward.

items.title: Forms routed to reps
items.body: A web form becomes a CRM record with its source attached and duplicates merged.

items.title: Automations and AI agents
items.body: Routine steps run as documented rules: a missed call becomes a callback task, a booked call lands on the record.

items.title: Calling and email connected
items.body: A business calling platform is connected to the CRM so each call is logged on the record with its recording.

items.title: Dashboards and a revenue scoreboard
items.body: Targets per rep and per team, a live leaderboard of calls, booked meetings and closed sales, and the owner's view of pipeline and revenue.

items.title: Data moved over, team trained
items.body: Your data is migrated from the current system or spreadsheets, with duplicates merged. Training sessions run on your own data and are recorded for the team.

blocks.h2: When monday CRM fits, and when a heavier CRM does.
blocks.intro: The right CRM is the one your reps keep current.

items.title: Your sales process is easy to draw
items.body: A lead comes in, a rep qualifies it, a quote goes out, and the sale closes or it does not.

items.title: Your company already works in monday.com
items.body: When the people your reps hand work to already use monday.com, a CRM from the same vendor is a reasonable place to start.

items.title: Nobody is a full-time CRM admin
items.body: If the person who maintains the CRM also runs the team, a setup with fewer moving parts is easier to keep current.

items.title: When a heavier CRM is the better fit
items.body: A heavier CRM tends to fit when several departments share one system, a dedicated admin runs it, or the process has many exceptions and approval layers.

items.title: HubSpot vs monday CRM
items.body: HubSpot and monday CRM are both on the list of CRMs we set up, alongside Close, Nutshell, Capsule and HighLevel.

items.title: When the vendor's onboarding is enough
items.body: Some teams need no consultant. If the vendor's own onboarding is enough for your case, we say so.

blocks.h2: What a monday.com consultant does, step by step.
blocks.intro: A monday.com consultant, sometimes called a monday.com expert, turns a new account into a working sales system.

items.title: A free first call
items.body: We go through what you use today, what isn't working, and what you are trying to get to.

items.title: A written proposal
items.body: The proposal sets out the tools and why, the monthly software cost, the implementation scope, the fixed fee and what counts as done.

items.title: The purchase, through us or direct
items.body: Where it helps, we set the plan and seats up through the vendor's program, in your name, and apply any customer offer it provides.

items.title: The build
items.body: Your consultant works inside your account through an admin seat you create and can revoke at handover.

items.title: Data moved over
items.body: Records come across from your current system or spreadsheets, with duplicates merged. The old system stays read-only during the switch, then it is yours to close.

items.title: Training and handover
items.body: Your team is trained on the setup, on your own data, and the sessions are recorded.

blocks.intro: There are two separate numbers, and both are on the proposal: what the software costs you each month, and what our work costs.

items.title: The software: per seat
items.body: monday CRM is priced per seat, on monday.com's own plans. Your cost depends on the plan and the number of seats.

items.title: Partner program offers, shown
items.body: Where a vendor partner program provides a customer offer, it is applied and shown on the proposal. Where none exists, you pay the vendor's own price.

items.title: Implementation: a fixed fee
items.body: Stacktik's implementation work is scoped and quoted as a fixed fee, in writing, before it starts.

items.title: Software and setup are separate
items.body: You can buy the software direct and hire us only for the implementation, or buy through us and run the setup yourself.

items.title: Ongoing support: optional
items.body: Monthly support is for teams that want the people who built the system to keep it current. It is optional.

platforms.intro: The CRM is the system the others connect to.

faq.a: monday CRM, also written monday.com CRM, is the sales CRM from monday.com. It is where a sales team keeps every customer, opportunity and conversation, on boards with a pipeline, forms, automations and dashboards.

faq.q: How does monday CRM pricing work?
faq.a: monday CRM is priced per seat, on monday.com's own plans, so the cost depends on the plan you choose and how many people need a seat. Stacktik's proposal shows the monthly software cost for your seat count and how it is billed.

faq.q: How does a monday.com implementation work?
faq.a: It runs as a free first call, a written proposal, then the build. The proposal sets the scope, the order of the steps, what we need from your team and what counts as done.

faq.q: HubSpot vs monday CRM: how do we choose?
faq.a: Choose on how your team sells and what each option costs you a month, not on demos. Stacktik sets up both. We map how leads, calls and follow-ups move through your team, then put the CRMs that fit on a written proposal with the monthly cost of each.

faq.q: Do we need a monday.com partner or consultant to set up monday CRM?
faq.a: No. Some teams set it up themselves, and if the vendor's own onboarding is enough for your case, we say so. A consultant helps when the CRM has to work with calling, outreach and reporting tools as one system.

faq.q: Can you move our data into monday CRM from spreadsheets or another CRM?
faq.a: Yes. Data migration from your current system or spreadsheets is part of what an implementation can include, with duplicates merged on the way in. The old system stays read-only during the switch, then it is yours to close.

closeLede: A free first call about what you use today and what isn't working.
